dk_values.method: Note (1): process Dk of 4 mil RO4350B laminates; the note states no condition of its own, and the process row it qualifies is defined at 10 GHz and 23 °C by IPC-TM-650 2.5.5.5
Differential phase length method, z direction; note (2): average of several tested lots on the most common thickness(es)

notes: The column header calls all values typical, and the text below the table describes typical values as an average for the population and refers to Rogers for specification values. Thermal coefficient of εr: +50 ppm/°C from -50 °C to 150 °C (IPC-TM-650 2.5.5.5). Moisture absorption: 0.06 % (48 h immersion, 0.060 in sample, 50 °C, ASTM D570). The table gives Dk only at 10 GHz (process) and for 8 to 40 GHz (design); Chart 2 on page index 1 gives the frequency dependence from 1 GHz upward (next record). revision: Revised 1687 013024, Publication #92-130, (c) 2024 Rogers Corporation (printed on page index 3)
location: Chart 3: Normalized Dk vs. Frequency using microstrip differential phase length method, 50 ohm microstrip circuits based on ~20 mil thick laminates (logarithmic axis 1 to 50 GHz)
notes: The chart plots normalized Dk, not Dk, and does not state the frequency at which the curves are normalized; all curves cross 1.00 near 20 to 25 GHz. Read by eye (major gridlines every 0.01, reading resolution about ±0.002), the RO3003 curve is about 1.010 at 1 GHz, 1.005 at 2 GHz and 1.001 at 10 GHz, so the chart puts the RO3003 microstrip Dk at 1 GHz about 1 % above its 10 GHz value. The 'High Performance FR-4' curve on the same chart is about 1.041 at 1 GHz and 1.011 at 10 GHz. Nothing below 1 GHz is plotted. Chart 1 on the same page plots the normalized RO3003 and RO3035 dielectric constant against temperature from -50 °C to 150 °C.
